Weather data from Crossnacreevy, made easier to explore

crossmet is an R package for importing, summarising and visualising daily meteorological observations from the AFBI Crossnacreevy weather station in Northern Ireland.

Use the package to move from annual Excel worksheets to tidy observations, year-by-year monthly summaries, long-term monthly climate summaries and publication-ready plots.

Import

Read the relevant annual worksheets, validate the workbook structure and return a tidy long-format data frame.

Importing guide

Summarise

Compare individual years with `MonthlySummaryTable()` or calculate monthly climate normals with `ClimateSummaryTable()`.

Summary guide

Visualise

Explore daily time series and a calendar-style grid of each month’s daily weather observations.

Graph gallery

Start here 

install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("GABurns/crossmet")

library(crossmet)

weather <- ImportWeather(
  file = "path/to/crossnacreevy.xlsx",
  start_date = "2020-01-01",
  end_date = "2024-12-31"
)

monthly <- MonthlySummaryTable(weather)
climate <- ClimateSummaryTable(weather)

RainfallPlot(weather)

The workbook is expected to contain one worksheet per year, named with its four-digit year, and the Crossnacreevy weather-station column layout.

About the data

The package is designed around daily station summaries. It does not replace quality control or metadata from the station operator. Check the source workbook, instrument metadata and observation coverage before interpreting long-term trends or comparing variables across periods.
